title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the surrounding pages (§50 ff. of the sequel to La Longue Marche): Π_0 is a discrete group. In this Galois–Teichmüller context it is presumably a Teichmüller-type or surface-type group, but that is my inference. T_0 ≅ Z, and k_i : T_0 → Π_0 are distinguished 'inertia' homomorphisms; Dehn-twist or cusp generators are my guess. On the previous page Grothendieck asks for a smooth model Π (underlined) over Z of an algebraic envelope Π_Q. It should come with M = M(Z) and a character χ_M to G_m. Over Z the k_i need not extend to homomorphisms T_0 (as a group scheme) → Π. So he passes to the centralizer L̃_{i,0} = Centr_{Π_0}(k_i), an arithmetic group. The map L̃_{i,0} → Π(Z) is 'continuously unipotent', so by §50, 4° (p. 658' ff.) it factors through his Z-envelope Env(L̃_{i,0}) → Π (formula 51).

This page: (51) factors further through one of the smooth quotient group schemes Z_{i,n} of Env(L̃_{i,0}). These sit in an extension (52) 1 → nT_0 (underlined) → Z_{i,n} → (H_{i,n})_{Spec Z} → 1. Here H_{i,n} ≅ L̃_{i,0}/nT_0 is a constant group scheme, possibly infinite, so the scheme is only locally of finite type. The identity component Z_{i,n}^0 is the Z-model of G_a whose Z-points are the lattice nT_0. In concrete terms it is G_a with coordinate x/n relative to the generator of T_0. So Z_{i,n} is a Z-model of the 'Malcev-plus-discrete' envelope of the centralizer, in which the inertia line T_0 is replaced by an integral form of G_a.

Next he restricts the induced map Z_{i,n} → Π to the identity component nT_0 ≅ G_a. This restriction is generally not a monomorphism. If it is a mono for n, it fails for every proper multiple n' of n. The reason is that the transition map between the n'- and n-models is x ↦ (n'/n)x on G_a. This has an infinitesimal kernel in characteristic p dividing n'/n, so it is not a mono over Z.

The 'favourable' case (53) is when some n makes nT_0 → Π a mono. That should mean the schematic closure in Π of the generic one-parameter additive subgroup k_i(G_{a,Q}) is a smooth subgroup scheme of Π. Such a closure is then necessarily ≅ G_a: the fibres over F_p are perfect fields, so no nontrivial forms of G_a occur, and dilatations just rescale the coordinate.

The next page states the converse, with a condition on the identity component. It then gets a unique-up-to-conjugacy closed embedding K'_i : T_0 (as group scheme) ↪ Π with generic fibre K_{i,Q}∘(r_i·id), r_i ∈ Q*_+. Factorization through Π_0 on Z-points is added as an extra hypothesis.

Purpose: to give an integral (over Spec Z) structure theory for algebraic envelopes of the discrete group in which the inertia subgroups become integral copies of G_a. Normalizing these copies singles out canonical rescalings of the inertia homomorphisms.
errors: 'End(L̃_{i,0})' must be Env(L̃_{i,0}), the envelope of formula (51).

The phrase '(53) mono ⇒ schematic closure smooth' needs the mono to be a closed immersion. For flat finite-type groups over Z, a monomorphism need not be a closed immersion in general. For G_a with smooth affine target it is fine, but this is not argued. Grothendieck himself flags the extra condition on the identity component on the next page.
H_{i,n} ≅ L̃_{i,0}/nT_0 is generally infinite (L̃ is an arithmetic group). So Z_{i,n} is only locally of finite type. 'Lisse' must be understood in that sense; this is not stated.

ideas.what: Smooth quotients Z_{i,n} of the Z-envelope of the centralizer of an inertia generator, extensions of a constant (possibly infinite) group by an integral G_a-model nT_0
ideas.modern_name: integral models of relative/Malcev completions; smooth models of G_a and group schemes locally of finite type with constant component group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Malcev (rational unipotent completion); Deligne, Hain (relative completion over Q or Q_ℓ); no standard integral theory
ideas.where_published: Unpublished; continuation of La Longue Marche (1981), §50

ideas.what: Mono-ness of G_a-models fails under rescaling by n'/n: x ↦ (n'/n)x has kernel in characteristic p
ideas.modern_name: dilatations / Néron-type models of G_a over Z

ideas.what: Criterion: the schematic closure in Π of the generic one-parameter subgroup k_i(G_{a,Q}) is smooth iff some integral rescaling of the inertia line embeds; this yields canonical rational rescalings r_i of the inertia homomorphisms
ideas.modern_name: schematic closure of a one-parameter unipotent subgroup in an integral model; integral normalization of the logarithm of inertia
ideas.usually_credited_to: no standard attribution in this setting

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches a program of smooth Z-models of algebraic envelopes of (Teichmüller-type) discrete groups, in which inertia subgroups become closed integral G_a's. Smoothness of the schematic closure of each inertia one-parameter subgroup is the test, and canonical scalings r_i ∈ Q*_+ come out of it. Integral (over Spec Z rather than Q or Q_ℓ) relative completions of mapping class groups with integral inertia lines do not seem to have been developed.
missed.quote: Cela indique que l'adhérence schématique dans Π du "sous-groupe additif à 1 paramètre" ... est un sous-schéma en groupes lisse de Π.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Relative completions of mapping class groups (Hain, Matsumoto) and the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group are studied over Q or Q_ℓ. An integral model with normalized inertia lines could constrain integral and torsion phenomena, for example the denominators appearing in GT and in Drinfeld associators.

deep.surprise_reason: Unpublished and fairly specific: a Z-integral envelope theory with discrete component groups, plus a smoothness criterion for the closure of inertia lines. But the local mathematics on this page (G_a models, rescaling kernels) is standard, and the thread is only sketched.
